title: HNSW add_reverse_edge pure-distance pruning orphans near-duplicate cluster members (recall loss)
wanted_capability: Connectivity-preserving reverse-edge pruning in HnswIndex. add_reverse_edge (crates/bbox-vectors/src/hnsw.rs:404) prunes a saturated neighbor list purely by distance, so in a near-duplicate cluster larger than m0 (=64) later members evict earlier members from every inbound list — in-degree drops to 0 and the node becomes unreachable by search (search_layer/greedy_closest only follow forward edges from the entry point). Reproduced: 20 clusters x 1000 members (sigma 0.05), sequential push (prod's incremental arrival order) → 5,685/20,000 disconnected (28%), zero-in-degree 5,684 (exact match — orphaning IS the mechanism), self-recall misses 350/1000 (35% of indexed vectors not returned in their own top-10). Bulk build (level-sorted) still loses 913/20,000 (4.6%). Prod partition voyage-voyage-code-3-1024-0103683e currently reports 66,621/399,613 disconnected (~17%) — transcript corpora are near-duplicate-heavy, so this is live recall loss, not a metric artifact. Wanted fix: apply the select_neighbors diversity heuristic when shrinking the reverse-edge list (HNSW paper's shrink-connections), optionally with keep-pruned-connections, instead of distance-sort-truncate; plus a regression test asserting self-recall under large-cluster sequential push. After the fix, prod needs an HNSW rebuild (bbox_reembed or partition rebuild) to repair existing graphs.
fallback_used: None — the large ef_search floor (max(len/4, 2000)-capped) partially masks the loss for well-connected regions, but orphaned nodes are unreachable at any ef.
evidence: crates/bbox-vectors/src/hnsw.rs:351 (search skips inactive only; forward-edge traversal)
repro: 20x1000 clusters sigma=0.05 push-order -> disconnected 5685/20000, zero_in 5684, self-recall miss 350/1000, bulk-build 913/20000
resolution_note: Fix shipped (commit b236f50) and both prod partitions rebuilt through it. add_reverse_edge now shrinks saturated inbound lists with the select_neighbors diversity heuristic (SHRINK-CONNECTIONS; the distance backfill doubles as keep-pruned-connections). Synthetic repro: 5,685/20,000 disconnected + 35% self-recall miss → 0 disconnected / 99.7% self-recall on both push and bulk paths. Live rebuilds (rebuild_hnsw workflow op → Partition::compact): Linux host 66,621/399,613 (16.7%) → 5,516/399,136 (1.38%); Mac mini 6,417/95,973 (6.7%) → 287/95,979 (0.30%). Residual disconnection is exact-duplicate degeneracy — identical chunks embedded under different entity ids tie all pairwise distances at zero, so the diversity rule cannot discriminate; orphaning there is mostly benign (the surviving twin answers the query). Full elimination would need a post-build orphan-reconnect pass — file separately if the residual ever matters. Diagnostics added alongside (HnswMetrics.zero_in_degree_nodes, self_recall_probe) attributed the disconnection exactly (zero_in == disconnected) on every measurement. Regression test: large_near_duplicate_clusters_stay_connected_under_push_order fails at 167/1200 on the old pruning, passes <1% + self-recall >=0.98 with the fix.
